answer: Anchor trust in the honest core of the social graph and let it diffuse by short random walks: each walk starts at an established member and follows real interaction edges, so identities on a sparsely connected island of fake accounts are rarely visited. A knoll of Sybils may link densely among themselves, but the few edges crossing to honest members bottleneck their score. Every new fake identity must therefore buy or earn genuine ties to established members, a cost paid per identity that cannot be shared or amortized across copies.
